title: Anastomotic leakage in gynecologic oncologic surgery
summary:
Background: Anastomotic leakage is one of the most serious complications associated with gynecologic oncology surgery.

Research Question: How frequently does anastomotic leakage occur, and are there potential risk factors that may contribute to its development, such as the surgical technique used, the volume of fluids administered, comorbidities, duration of surgery, or patient age?

Methods: Retrospective data collection from existing medical records, focusing on the primary endpoint: the occurrence of anastomotic leakage.
conditions: Insufficiency of anastomoses and sutures following surgery on other parts of the digestive tract.

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of all anastomoses performed in Gynecologic Oncology at the University Hospital Bonn between January 2015 and September 2026.
